pairs.question: Quare enim iste usus fructus sibi tale vindicat privilegium, ut generali interemptione usus fructus ipse solus excipiatur?
pairs.answer: Quod ex nulla induci rationabili sententia manifestissimum est.
pairs.derivation: Prose legal text; authorial rhetorical question and its own answer. Stripped the section marker (CJ.3.33.14.1: Imperator Justinianus) and the trailing subscript apparatus (<a 530 d. xv k. oct. lampadio et oreste vv. cc. conss.>). The question is the freestanding interrogative; preceding it is the ruling 'tales altercationes decidentes censemus ... expirare.', which is exposition not needed for the question to be intelligible, so it was not included. The answer is the next independent sentence, which genuinely answers (the privilege rests on no reasonable principle). Capitalization of the answer's first word normalized.

pairs.question: Quare enim, si filius familias fuerit is qui usum fructum habet, forte ex castrensi peculio, ubi nec usus fructus adquiritur ei, possessum, per emancipationem eum amittat?
pairs.answer: Sed secundum quod definitum est tunc eum tantummodo desinere, cum usufructuarius vel res pereat, et tantummodo eum cum anima vel rei substantia expirare, nisi praedictae exceptionis vigor reclamaverit.
pairs.derivation: Prose legal text; authorial rhetorical question with its own answer. Stripped the section marker (CJ.3.33.16.2: Imperator Justinianus) and the trailing subscript apparatus (<a 530 d. k. oct. ... conss.>). The preceding sentence 'Sed nec per omnem capitis deminutionem ... subiectis.' is general framing not needed for the question, so it was not included. The answer is the reply's independent sentence (beginning 'Sed secundum quod definitum est'), taken to the first full stop, which genuinely answers the 'why should he lose it' (he loses it only on death/destruction, not by emancipation). First word capitalization normalized.
